name: Question 4
problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and ${a}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $A.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${a}_{3}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$ 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(A)$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${a}_{3}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{(-1)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=(-1)\cdot 3=-3.$

Question 4
?

The matrix A is given below. Let a1, a2, and a3 be the respective columns of A. Determine if B={a1,a2} is a basis of Col(A). If that is the case, find x1⋅x2, where a3=x1a1+x2a2.

A=[10−10−2−6]

a
35
b
3
c
1
d
−3
e
{a1,a2} is not a basis of Col(A)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we reduce the matrix A to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

A=[10−10−2−6]R2:=−12R2∼[10−1013]

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the 1st and 2nd columns. So, a basis of Col(A) is {a1,a2}, that is to say,

B={[10],[0−2]}.

Now, since the 3rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express a3 as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

[−1−6]⏟a3=(−1)⏟x1⋅[10]⏟a1+(3)⏟x2⋅[0−2]⏟a2.

This gives us x1⋅x2=(−1)⋅3=−3.
